what: Patching Codex's installed files at start-up, the prompt to reload, and Remove the Patch putting Codex's own files back until Turn On reapplies it
The work plan plugin installed into Codex, trust for its hooks, and the commands that install it again, download Python, trust the hooks and stop Codex loading it
Codex Plus's Codex button on the editor tab bar in place of Codex's own, opening a new conversation in a tab or Codex's sidebar as codexPlus.tabBarButton says
A Codex tab's title following the conversation's name, including a conversation started in a tab

The dot on a Codex tab's logo by what the conversation is doing: a green dot while a turn runs, a green ring while only something it started still runs, red while it waits for permission, and none once it has stopped
A Codex tab's right-click menu with Rename, Mark as Unread and Add to Group
The Recently closed section of the session list, listing conversations whose tabs were closed
Ctrl+Shift+T reopening the Codex conversation closed last while the tab closed last was a Codex tab
Reopening the Codex tabs VS Code did not restore after the window lost its remote connection
notInWindow: Needs a Remote SSH window whose connection drops and comes back; this window is local and has none to lose.

what: The Codex sessions view in the Codex Plus sidebar: Account & usage, Open sessions, the session manager with New in tab and New in sidebar, groups and Ungrouped, each row with dot, title and time
New in tab and New in sidebar in the session list, starting a Codex conversation

Account & usage at the top of the session list: how Codex is signed in, and rate limits and tokens when Codex gives them; the window shows only that the section is left out while Codex reports no account, since a real sign-in needs the network
A row's hover in the session list naming its group, session ID and what it still runs
The status dot on each row of the session list by what the conversation is doing: a green dot running, a green ring with only background work left, red waiting, and none stopped

The envelope after a conversation's title for a reply not seen: at the end of its tab's title and after the title on its rows in the session list, never saved into its name by Rename, and kept whole after the ellipsis of a long title in a narrow side bar
The session list's search box, filtering rows and marking the matched part of each title
The status filter menu (Needs input, Working, Completed, Open, Closed with counts) and the Active button
The session list's own right-click menu on a row, drawn in the look of Claude Code's
Resume in Tab and Resume in Sidebar on a row, opening the conversation in a Codex tab or in Codex's sidebar
Text Color on a row: a submenu of Default and eight colours, colouring the row's title
Renaming a conversation where its title is drawn in the list
Groups in the session list: New group, Add to Group, the group header's menu, renaming and deleting a group, Remove from Group, Start New Session in This Group
Mark as Unread and Mark as Read on a row, changing Codex Plus's record of what was read
Find a Codex Conversation by Title or ID, a quick pick over this workspace's conversations
Listing the conversations Codex starts by itself, such as sub-agents, indented under the conversation that started them once codexPlus.hideBackgroundSessions is off
Archive and Unarchive, the collapsed Archived sessions group, the archived row's menu, and Delete with its confirmation
Deleting, once a day, conversations archived at least codexPlus.deleteArchivedAfterDays days ago
notInWindow: Runs once a day on conversations archived 30 or more days ago; the made-up Codex home has none that old, and the sweep shows only lines in the output channel.

what: A conversation archived while its tab is open keeping its turns read-only with no message box, and getting the box back once opened from the list
A conversation's goal shown on its row, and Pause Goal, Resume Goal and Clear Goal in the row's menu and the Agent map
The time above every message and reply block in a Codex conversation
Beside each reply's time its context share, model and effort, and the turn's duration when Codex shows no Worked for
The row below the message box naming the tool call running now and counting commands still running
The rail at the right edge listing your own messages by time and opening words, and the box beside a row on hover
Your own messages marked with a bar down their leading edge, and coloured by codexPlus.userMessageColor
A Stop hook's prompt in the conversation folded to one dim line, unfolded on a click
The four controls Codex Plus puts in the message box's toolbar: information button, note button, context meter and Agent map
The information button opening the conversation's thread ID, app-server, folder, rollout, context, tokens, account and token mode
Chimes on a finished turn, a question and a permission stop, and the note button that turns them on and off, struck through while off
The context meter in the toolbar, its hover with the window and where it came from, and a click starting a compaction
An outline round the context meter once 80% or more of the context window is used
The Agent map pill and its dialog listing the wake-up, the goal, sub-agents and detached commands
Images in replies drawn at their own size from absolute paths, file:// and data: URLs, web images shown as links, and [Image] with codexPlus.replyImages off
The installed skills that best fit a message, given to Codex before the turn and named on the line above the reply
Searching skills by meaning through cohere.embed-v4 on Amazon Bedrock
notInWindow: Runs only while Codex's provider is Amazon Bedrock, and needs Bedrock credentials and the network; the window runs offline against a made-up model.

what: Searching the skills of Claude Code plugins named in codexPlus.skillRoutingClaudePlugins
notInWindow: Needs Claude Code plugins installed in the made-up home; with none the setting changes nothing on screen.

what: Codex's own list of skills: its budget and the skills it leaves out, written into Codex's config.toml
notInWindow: Both only write config.toml entries that change what Codex sends the model; nothing Codex Plus draws changes.

what: A wake-up the model set being sent into the idle conversation when it is due, as a message with its own first line
A conversation keeping a green ring after its turn while a background command, a sub-agent or a detached command it started is still running
The notice sent into the conversation once a detached command it started stops
A conversation stopped for Codex's approval shown as waiting: Codex's card, the red dot on its tab and its row
Agent Plus's Work plan view showing the plan of the Codex conversation in front
Codex conversations in Agent Plus's Conversations view, with their state and the questions in their plans
The conversation's brief, its summary and status, shown in Agent Plus's Answer view on a click of its row
Answering a plan question in Agent Plus's Answer view, the answer typed into the conversation's message box and sent
Agent Plus's notification when a conversation finishes behind another tab, and the count beside the bell in the status bar, listing them on a click
Agent Plus's token mode entry in the status bar: its hover, the list of modes and the switch to another
Show Status writing what is installed, patched and running to the Codex Plus output channel
Show How Long Opening a Codex Page Took, from Codex's own log
Turn Off, Turn On and Toggle On/Off over everything Codex Plus draws in Codex's page and tabs
Codex Plus: Settings, opening VS Code's settings filtered to this extension
Telling Codex the user's time zone when Codex runs on another machine
notInWindow: Only adds a note to what Codex sends the model, and only when Codex runs on another machine; nothing in the window changes.

what: The work plan's reminders at the end of a turn and around a compaction, the offer of a plan, and the pattern that silences them
notInWindow: These change only what the plugin's hooks send the model. A reminder that does reach the conversation is shown as a Stop hook's prompt, which hook-prompt-fold covers.
